comparator.name: Information Science (Informatiekunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The programme-specific 2026-2027 TER, adopted on 7 July 2026, defines the redesigned 180-EC curriculum for students starting in September 2026. Table 3 supplies a fixed 60-EC first year, a fixed 60-EC second year beginning in 2027-2028, and a third year beginning in 2028-2029 with a 30-EC minor and 30 EC of compulsory ethics, co-creative AI, data-science project and thesis work. The older second- and third-year courses shown in the 2026-2027 Ocasys transition display apply to earlier cohorts and are not used here. The genuine minor space remains open.

alternatives.label: AI, information & human-centred technology
alternatives.concept: Combines programming, databases, data science and machine learning with user-centred design, cognitive science, language processing, search and responsible AI. It follows Groningen's applied, human-centred information-science orientation while acknowledging UCR's broader interdisciplinary structure and more limited dedicated language-technology sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum gives sustained space to applied AI and information processing while integrating user interaction, language and responsible technology.
progression: Programming, data, research and human-behaviour foundations precede advanced databases, machine learning, algorithms, user interaction, neural networks and language processing. The enriched workbook confirms prerequisites and assigned 2026-2029 terms; seven 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Law, AI & digital governance
alternatives.concept: Retains programming, databases, data science, machine learning and user-oriented design but organizes the advanced programme around rights, international and EU law, constitutional governance, responsibility and ethical technology. This develops the programme's explicit Law and IT direction without claiming a professional law degree.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines a substantial information-technology core with a sustained legal and ethical governance strand.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, nine courses shift toward law and digital governance; compared with the business route, eight courses differ. Each pair therefore exceeds the 30-EC/four-course threshold.
progression: Programming, data, research and law-and-society foundations precede databases, machine learning, algorithms, EU, criminal, private and constitutional law, AI and applied evaluation. The enriched workbook confirms prerequisites and planned terms; six 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Business information systems & AI
alternatives.concept: Retains programming, databases, data science, machine learning and responsible AI while shifting the programme toward digital transformation, organisational behaviour, user markets, leadership, strategy and financial decisions. This develops the programme's explicit Business Information Science direction.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines an information-systems and AI core with sustained organisational, strategic and business analysis.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest match, seven courses shift toward business and organisations; compared with the law route, eight courses differ. Each pair therefore exceeds the 30-EC/four-course threshold.
progression: Programming, data, research and business foundations precede databases, machine learning, digital transformation, organisational leadership, algorithms, AI and market research. The enriched workbook confirms prerequisites and planned terms; eight 300-level courses are included.

candidates.label: Business information science and digital organisations

selection.assessment: The closest match integrates all direct generator interests across applied AI, data, human-centred technology, responsible information processing, language technology, search and conversational systems. In production order, the explicit Law and IT and Business Information Science directions each support a coherent additional curriculum with material course consequences and pairwise differences of at least 30 EC. Production therefore stops at the permitted maximum of three; the later AI, Linguistics and Communication directions are recorded but not separately instantiated.

blocks: Introduction to Programming directly addresses the programming foundation, with different language, scope and credits.
Introduction to Data Science directly addresses data manipulation and analysis, with broader introductory scope.
Database Management Systems directly addresses database design and query processing, with different scope and credits.
Logic & Discrete Mathematics supplies formal foundations for information processing but not the full information-theory syllabus.
Machine Learning directly addresses the compulsory machine-learning component, with different scope and credits.
Algorithms & Data Structures supports efficient search and retrieval, but is not a dedicated search-engines course.
Optimization Methods in AI contributes AI search and agent problem-solving, but does not reproduce co-creative AI.
Neural Networks & Deep Learning directly addresses neural models and includes text classification and generative AI.
UCR has no selected dedicated web-development course.
UCR has applied data projects within courses, but no selected separate 10-EC data-science project.
Introduction to Sociology supports analysis of technology in society but does not reproduce the integrated Humane AI course.
Consumer Product Design uses user-needs analysis, prototyping and iteration relevant to usability and UX.
Style & Meaning develops analysis of language and interpretation relevant to language-technology foundations.
Perception & Action supplies human sensorimotor foundations for interaction, but not a dedicated human-robot course.
Psycholinguistics directly studies language production and comprehension, though without the full computational-processing scope.
UCR has no selected single disciplinary introduction to Information Science.
UCR integrates responsible human-centred projects across courses but has no selected equivalent 10-EC Humane AI project module.
Research Methods & Statistics directly supplies statistical and research foundations, with different scope and credits.
AI Ethics addresses ethical and societal issues in information technology, with an AI-specific emphasis.
The genuine 30-EC minor space is preserved without inventing a Groningen minor selection.
UCR's optional independent-research opportunity is shown separately against the compulsory thesis; it is not part of the fixed 180-EC UCR curricula.

notes.text: UCR offers substantial programming, databases, data science, machine learning, AI ethics, user-centred design, cognitive science and language-related study, but it does not reproduce Groningen's full compulsory web-development, natural-language-processing, human-robot-interaction, co-creative-AI and information-science project sequence.
